reader.requirement: At 1985 the logical pages of a LINAGE file (top margin + page body + bottom margin, from integers or data-names re-read at each page transition) are laid end to end on the medium with no lines or form feeds between them, for page overflow on AFTER and BEFORE advancing, for ADVANCING PAGE, with and without margins and FOOTING. The witness covers AFTER ADVANCING overflow with literal margins only.

reader.notes: BeginNextLogicalPage travels the rest of the body plus the bottom margin, re-evaluates the operands, then exactly one line onto the next page's line 1, and the next top margin follows; a LINAGE file never takes the form-feed arm. The output is the same at --std 85 and --std 2023, and the LINAGE path consults no edition.

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-022/r6lin-001 at --std 85, the arms the reader did not try, read off the produced files byte for byte: (1) LINAGE 5 TOP 2 BOTTOM 1 (8-line pages), three AFTER 1 writes on lines 4-6, then AFTER ADVANCING 4 overflowing -> A4 on line 11 (page 2 = lines 9-16, body line 1), then AFTER ADVANCING 9 (more than a page body) -> A5 on line 19 (page 3 body line 1), no page skipped and no form feed; (2) LINAGE 3 TOP 1 BOTTOM 1, four BEFORE 1 writes -> lines 2,3,4 then 7 (BEFORE overflow with both margins); (3) LINAGE 3 TOP 1 BOTTOM 2, BEFORE ADVANCING PAGE then BEFORE 2 overflowing and AFTER 0 -> B1 line 2, B2 line 8, B3 line 10, B4 line 14; (4) LINAGE 4 BOTTOM 2 with AFTER ADVANCING PAGE as the first write -> C1 on line 7, C2 on line 13. Every page boundary falls at a multiple of the logical page size, as §1985:VII.4.7.4 GR16g and the automatic-overflow paragraph place each record. r6lin-002 at --std 2023 writes byte-identical files (cmp).
